event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing reflects that, four years after the official declaration of COVID-19 as a global pandemic, STZ continues to view health-crisis-related disruptions as a live, but now medium-term, enterprise-wide risk.  The company discloses both historical impacts ("have resulted") and forward-looking exposures ("could result") across consumer demand, supply-chain logistics, workforce availability, and financial markets.  Language is largely qualitative—no dollar amounts or quantified volume impacts are provided—but it is still specific, citing venue closures, quarantines, border shutdowns, and uninsured losses.  Severity is underlined by repeated references to "material adverse effect," yet the text offers little in the way of concrete mitigations beyond general awareness.  Applying the Time-Decay Principle, the pandemic sits at the 4-year mark, so evidence scores must be moderated (4-6 range for the strongest sentences, tapering downward for ancillary mentions).  Overall, the pandemic remains a meaningful, but no longer acute, risk driver for STZ.

evidence_list.snippet: Communicable disease outbreaks, including the COVID-19 pandemic, and other widespread public health crises have resulted and in the future could result in disruptions and damage to our business caused by potential negative consumer purchasing behavior and reduced consumption as well as disruption to our supply chains, production processes, and operations.

components.reason: Explicitly references the COVID-19 pandemic by name.
States that the pandemic HAS ALREADY caused disruptions (‘have resulted’), indicating realised impact.
Enumerates multiple critical areas affected (consumer demand, supply chain, production, operations).
Medium-term time decay adjustment (event ~4 yrs old).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, multi-faceted statement of both historical and future pandemic impacts merits the maximum medium-term score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: This includes containment actions that restrict consumer purchasing occasions, including from the inability to leave home or otherwise shop in a normal manner, cancellations of public events, venue closures, or capacity restrictions, as well as reductions in consumer discretionary income due to reduced or limited work and layoffs.

components.reason: Details specific containment measures (lockdowns, venue closures, capacity limits).
Highlights reduced consumer income and spending power.
Links measures directly to decreased purchasing occasions.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete mechanisms through which pandemics hurt demand, but lacks quantified impact; medium-term decay yields a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Supply disruption may result from restrictions on the ability of employees and others in the supply chain to travel and work, including from quarantines, individual illnesses, or border closures imposed by governments to deter the spread of communicable infections or diseases; determinations by us or our suppliers or distributors to temporarily suspend operations in affected areas; or other actions which restrict or otherwise negatively impact our ability to produce, package, and ship our products, our distributors’ ability to distribute our products, or our suppliers’ ability to provide us with raw, packaging, and other materials.

components.reason: Identifies specific supply-chain obstacles (quarantines, border closures).
Extends risk across company, suppliers, and distributors (broad scope).
Directly threatens production and shipping capabilities.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong coverage of supply-chain vulnerabilities keeps the score high, but moderated to 4 for event age.

evidence_list.snippet: Channels of entry may be closed or operate at reduced capacity, or transportation of product within a region or country may be limited.

components.reason: Highlights potential closure of entry channels and transport limits—critical logistics risk.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Brief, logistics-focused threat without context or magnitude; after decay adjustment the score is 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Our operations and the operations of our suppliers may become less efficient or otherwise be negatively impacted if our or their executive management or other key operational personnel are unable to work or if a significant percentage of our workforce is unable to work at all or at their normal production or other facility.

components.reason: Identifies workforce unavailability as a pandemic-linked operational risk.
Connects personnel absence to efficiency decline and negative impact.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges labor shortages but without quantification or severity terms; net score 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Another widespread health crisis or pandemic conditions could negatively affect the economies and financial markets of many countries resulting in a global economic downturn which could negatively impact demand for our products and our ability to borrow money.

components.reason: Flags macroeconomic and financing risks tied to future pandemics.
Specifies impact on product demand and borrowing capacity.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Macro-level risk statement with no historical data; moderated to a score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Any of these events could have a material adverse effect on our business, liquidity, financial condition, and/or results of operations.

components.reason: Uses strong severity language ('material adverse effect').
Aggregates previously listed pandemic impacts, signaling breadth.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Severity wording boosts importance, but generic phrasing and time decay restrain score to 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Our insurance policies do not cover certain types of catastrophes and may not cover certain events such as pandemics.

components.reason: Reveals an uninsured exposure specific to pandemics.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies coverage gap, but lacks detail on magnitude; after decay, score is 1.

evidence_list.snippet: We are more likely to experience a significant operational disruption or catastrophic loss in any one location from acts of war or terrorism, natural or man-made disasters, public health crises, labor strikes or other labor activities, cyberattacks and other attempts to penetrate our or our third-party service providers’ IT systems or the IT used by our non-production employees who work remotely, or unavailability of raw or packaging materials.

components.reason: Lists public health crises as a cause of significant operational disruption.
Notes additional complication from remote-work IT exposure.
Medium-term time decay adjustment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Brief mention of pandemic within broader risk list; minimal depth leads to score of 1.
